Main depression trial characteristics identify sunflower/fish-oil control arms in the Lucas and Lespérance studies. Preparation grade and an untreated oil control are unverified. Neither cohort provides a Parkinson depression result.
Included studies compare EPA or DHA and treatments or trial oil placebos. No fresh rosemary exposure with rated depressive symptoms was assigned.

The study tables identify corn-oil controls in the Carney and Jiang trials and a corn/soybean blend for Mazereeuw. Depression was scored in non-Parkinson cohorts without an independent refined corn-oil contrast.
Trials use omega-3 formulations or fish-oil capsules for clinical depression. They do not separately administer poached trout or provide a clinical Parkinson depression comparison.
Some trials use rapeseed in depression comparators. The report supplies no refined culinary canola treatment against Parkinson fatigue severity.
Cod or other fish oil products in references and supplement formulations cannot identify consumption of grilled cod or a Parkinson fatigue measure.
Sunflower-based blended comparators are listed. The Lespérance study examines comorbid anxiety as a moderator of depression, without a cold-pressed sunflower oil contrast for anxiety severity.
Park 2015 uses safflower oil plus oleic acid as a depression-trial comparator. The review does not give a separately treated cold-pressed oil with an anxiety severity endpoint.
The review summarizes fatty-acid intervention and comparator formulations. No virgin coconut oil arm reports clinical fatigue severity.
Corn oil appears as a comparator in depression trials. The synthesized comparisons do not isolate refined corn oil for pain severity.
Olive oil is used in depression comparator capsules in multiple included trials. Neither their processing grade nor a matching cold-pressed oil anxiety contrast is available.
Sunflower oil with a small amount of fish oil is a comparator for depressive symptoms. No identified refined sunflower oil estimate for clinical fatigue.
The study characteristics give no dried date fruit treatment arm and no clinical date-pain contrast.
Some included depression trials report cognitive findings, but no cold-pressed macadamia oil exposure was evaluated in the described trials.
The Jazayeri rapeseed and Bot rapeseed/MCT comparators provide some exposure context. The primary measures target mood and do not establish a cold-pressed canola effect on Parkinson anxiety.
The depression trial comparators are varied oil capsules. No refined coconut oil assignment supplies an executive-function result.
Marine fatty-acid supplements and comorbid anxiety are discussed, without assigning poached salmon or measuring a salmon effect on anxiety.
Corn-oil capsules appear in studies with depression outcomes. The review does not estimate refined corn oil effects on fatigue severity.
The report identifies sunflower/fish-oil depression controls, without a cold-pressed sunflower oil or executive-function comparison.
Rapeseed capsules are used as trial controls. The report concerns depression rather than a cold-pressed canola oil arm and Parkinson pain outcome.
Olive oil appears in depression controls. The source gives no extra-virgin oil preparation and insomnia comparison.
No cold-pressed macadamia oil treatment or corresponding anxiety score comparison appears in the included study characteristics.
